Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s vision or eyes.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child's hearing or ears.
Parent: He always turns the TV volume up really high. It's like he can't hear well unless it's blasting. I'm getting a bit concerned it could be a sign of a hearing problem.

Doctor: Please tell us about the problems with your child’s teeth.
Parent: We have to take him to the dentist a lot because his teeth are prone to problems. The dentist says he needs more frequent visits than average to keep them healthy.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s heart.
Parent: There's a structural issue with his heart that the doctors are monitoring. They say it's an abnormality that we should keep an eye on, but so far, it hasn't caused him any pain or discomfort.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's hormones.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any neurological problem your child has (brain, nerves, muscle tone, fits).
Parent: He seems a bit clumsy compared to other kids. When he runs or plays, he often trips or stumbles. The doctors mentioned it could be related to coordination issues.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child's kidneys.
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about any problems with your child’s immune system (ability to fight infection and vaccination responses).
Parent: N/A.

Doctor: Please tell us about problems with your child’s gastrointestinal system (feeding, stomach， bowel).
Parent: Constipation has been a real issue for our son. He struggles to go to the bathroom regularly and it causes him a lot of distress.

Doctor: Please use this box to tell us about any other medical problems that you haven’t been able to mention above.
Parent: He was born with shorter fingers than usual， which sometimes makes it tricky for him to hold onto things or do certain tasks that require finger dexterity.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at an increased risk of developing respiratory infections due to their immune system being more susceptible. Regular vaccinations and maintaining good hygiene practices are recommended to reduce the likelihood of respiratory tract infections.
- Monitoring for the presence of bronchiectasis, a condition characterized by persistent cough, sputum production, and recurrent pneumonia, is advised. Bronchodilator treatment may provide symptomatic relief in some cases.
- N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Your child experiences an increased susceptibility to respiratory infections due to their weakened immune system.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are at an increased risk of developing respiratory infections due to their immune system being more susceptible. Regular vaccinations and maintaining good hygiene practices are recommended to reduce the likelihood of respiratory tract infections.
- Monitoring for the presence of bronchiectasis, a condition characterized by persistent cough, sputum production, and recurrent pneumonia, is advised. Bronchodilator treatment may provide symptomatic relief in some cases.
- N/A

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Your child experiences constipation, which can make toileting difficult.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are more likely to experience constipation due to their immuno-suppressed state. Frequent toileting and dietary adjustments may alleviate symptoms.
- N/A

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Your child has a weaker immune system, increasing their vulnerability to infections.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to infections due to their weakened immune system. Regular vaccinations and maintaining good hygiene practices are crucial to reducing the likelihood of respiratory tract infections.
- Monitoring for the presence of bronchiectasis, a condition characterized by persistent cough, sputum production, and recurrent pneumonia, is advised. Bronchodilator treatment may provide symptomatic relief in some cases.
- N/A

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- Your child exhibits clumsiness, potentially indicating coordination issues.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome commonly exhibit developmental delays and behavioral differences. Neurological assessments and therapies aimed at improving fine motor control and cognitive function may offer benefits.
- N/A

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
- Your child faces challenges with swallowing and breathing, which can lead to nasal congestion and sinus issues.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome frequently encounter issues with swallowing and breathing, particularly infants. Nasal congestion and sinus issues are common and can exacerbate existing respiratory conditions.
- N/A

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
- Your child suffers from astigmatism, impacting their visual clarity.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Astigmatism is a common ocular condition affecting nearly all children with KBG syndrome. Regular eye examinations and appropriate corrective lenses can improve vision and reduce strain on the eyes.
- N/A

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- N/A

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- Your child requires frequent dental cleanings due to tooth sensitivity and potential issues.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to dental issues, including weak enamel and sensitivity to hot and cold temperatures. Regular dental check-ups and thorough cleaning are essential to prevent complications.
- N/A

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
- Your child shows signs of clumsiness, which impacts their ability to participate fully in physical activities and classroom play.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome frequently demonstrate developmental delays and behavioral differences. Education programs tailored to address cognitive, social, and emotional needs may enhance their overall academic performance and social integration.
- N/A

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
- Your child displays clumsiness, contributing to accidents and injuries during playtime.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome commonly exhibit developmental delays and behavioral differences. Behavioral interventions and therapeutic approaches aimed at enhancing cognitive, emotional, and social functions may positively impact their overall behavior and developmental trajectory.
- N/A

## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- Your child presents with brachydactyly, resulting in shortened fingers and a unique claw-like appearance.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome frequently display skeletal abnormalities, including short fingers (brachydactyly) with a curvature of the fifth digit (clinodactyly). An X-ray examination of the wrist (determined by bone age) and hip should be conducted to assess the lengthening capacity of the bones.
- N/A

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Regular dental check-ups: Conduct routine dental cleanings and ensure proper hygiene practices are followed to maintain oral health.
b) Regular hearing reviews: Schedule yearly audiometric evaluations starting at age five to detect and address auditory issues early.
c) Eyesight (ophthalmology) review: Arrange comprehensive ophthalmological examinations to identify and treat vision-related conditions promptly.
d) Consider a palate review: Given the prevalence of feeding difficulties and speech concerns, consulting a specialist for evaluation and possible intervention may be beneficial.
e) Cardiac review: Following diagnosis, conduct periodic cardiac evaluations to monitor for potential heart conditions, especially concerning the heart valves, chambers, and spinal cord.
f) Cranial ultrasound: Perform cranial ultrasounds to rule out anomalies such as hydrocephalus, brain malformations, and other congenital brain issues.
g) Orthopedic review: Conduct orthopedic assessments to evaluate the flexibility and strength of the child's limbs and joints, ensuring they are developing appropriately.
h) Immunizations: Maintain a strong immunization schedule to protect against various infectious diseases.
i) Vitamin D supplementation: Administer vitamin D supplements to boost the immune system and strengthen bones.
j) Nutritional assessment: Evaluate dietary intake and nutrient deficiencies, particularly calcium and vitamin D, to support overall health and immune function.
k) Speech therapy: Implement speech therapy programs to aid in communication and speech development.
l) Physical therapy: Incorporate physical therapy sessions to enhance muscle tone, flexibility, and coordination.
m) Occupational therapy: Introduce occupational therapy sessions to promote fine motor skill development and maximize functional abilities.
n) Behavioural therapy: Utilize behavioural therapy techniques to address behavioral and cognitive challenges.
o) Genetic counseling: Offer genetic counseling services to educate families about the condition and discuss options for future pregnancies.
p) Follow-up appointments: Attend scheduled follow-up appointments with specialists to monitor progress and adjust treatment plans as necessary.
q) Research participation: Encourage enrollment in clinical trials or observational studies to access novel treatments and protocols.
r) Parental education: Provide parental education workshops to equip caregivers with knowledge regarding managing the condition and promoting optimal care for their child.
s) Community resources: Advocate for community-based resources and support groups specifically targeted towards families dealing with similar conditions.
t) Long-term planning: Develop a detailed long-term care plan that includes considerations for future medical advancements, insurance coverage, financial planning, and legal matters pertinent to the condition.
u) Sleep apnea screening: Conduct sleep apnea screenings to identify and treat underlying respiratory conditions.
v) Thyroid function testing: Perform thyroid function tests to rule out hypothyroidism, which can contribute to immune suppression and developmental delays.
w) Vitamin D supplementation: Administer vitamin D supplements to bolster the immune system and fortify bones.
x) Bone density scans: Conduct bone density scans to monitor bone density and prevent fractures associated with the weakening of the immune system.
y) Sacroiliac joint injection: Consider sacroiliac joint injections to alleviate sacroiliac joint dysfunction, which can result from kyphosis or other skeletal anomalies.
z) Sacral dimple observation: Observe sacral dimple development to monitor for potential sacroiliac joint issues.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY

a) How this affects the patient:

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- N/A

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Around 38% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural abnormalities. Regular check-ups and monitoring are recommended.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Children with KBG syndrome commonly have feeding difficulties and swallowing issues, which can lead to aspiration pneumonia. They may also experience gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD).

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- People with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to infections due to their immune system being overactive. Vaccinations should be given according to the NHS schedule, but immunotherapy may be considered if there are frequent and severe reactions to vaccines.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Neurological features can vary widely between individuals. Common ones include seizures, learning difficulties, behavioral differences, and sensorineural hearing loss. Specific brain imaging (such as MRI) and genetic testing (for example, sequencing) might provide additional insights.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- KBG syndrome is associated with conductive hearing loss, which can result from various factors such as adenotonsillar hypertrophy, nasal congestion, and subtle palatal anomalies.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Vision-related issues can include astigmatism, shortsightedness (hypermetropia), and presbyopia (difficulty reading).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- N/A

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Teeth can be weak and sensitive, requiring careful brushing and dietary restrictions.

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Education needs vary greatly. Some children benefit from a more structured approach, while others thrive in a more free-flowing environment. Speech therapy and educational interventions tailored to the child’s unique challenges can significantly enhance their learning potential.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Behavioural differences are common, and therapies such as Applied Behavior Analysis (ABA), Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Sensory Integration Therapy (SET), and Parent Management Training (PMT) can offer valuable support.

## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
- N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
- Brachydactyly (short fingers) and clinodactyly (curved 5th finger) are typical features. Skeletal anomalies can include an unusual curvature of the spine (scoliosis) and hip dysplasia, which can cause gait issues and difficulty with activities requiring balance.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Regular dental check-ups.
b) Regular hearing reviews (beginning at age 5).
c) Eyesight (ophthalmology) review.
d) Consider a palate review (particularly if there are feeding difficulties or speech concerns).

f) Consider a skeletal review (X-ray of the wrist, hip, spine, and skull) in children following diagnosis.
g) Monitor growth velocity: if height is below the 2nd centile consider referral for endocrine investigations on an individual basis and within context of familial heights.
h) Work with a physiotherapist and occupational therapist to address musculoskeletal issues and sensory integration dysfunction.
i) Refer for consideration of a tethered cord review and investigation if sacral dimple is present.
j) Consider referral for speech therapy and audiological evaluations as appropriate.
k) Consider referral for neuropsychological assessments and behavioural therapy as appropriate.

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

    - Children with KBG syndrome commonly experience feeding difficulties and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), which can result in regurgitation and vomiting. They may also develop vitamin deficiencies due to poor appetite and absorption issues.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - People with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to developing autoimmune diseases and infections. They may require immunotherapy or additional vaccinations beyond the standard schedule.

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Neurological features can vary widely between individuals, but some common ones include seizures, developmental delays, behavioral differences, sensorineural hearing loss, and learning difficulties. Specific symptoms affecting the patient are:
        - Lack of coordination and imbalance when performing physical activities.
        - Delayed closure of the anterior fontanelle, indicating a unique cranial morphology characterized by a flattened occiput and triangular-shaped forehead.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - KBG syndrome is associated with conductive hearing loss, which can manifest as difficulty hearing high-pitched noises or distant voices. Sensorineural hearing loss, where damage occurs to the auditory nerve itself, has also been reported.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - People with KBG syndrome are more prone to vision-related issues such as astigmatism, shortsightedness (hypermetropia), and squint (strabismus).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Individuals with KBG syndrome may exhibit various dermatological features, including weak enamel on their teeth and frequent dental issues.

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Teeth characteristics such as large front teeth (macrodontia) and brachydactyly (shortened fingers) are common. Dental issues like weak enamel and susceptibility to cavities are also frequent.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Education outcomes can vary greatly. While most children with KBG syndrome attend mainstream primary schools, those with more significant learning challenges may require additional support in mainstream secondary schools or receive educational care.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Behavioural differences are quite common, including autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), anxiety, and sensory integration dysfunction. Learning difficulties can impact academic performance and the acquisition of motor skills.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Skeletal features can include short stature, irregular bone structures, and an unusual curvature of the spine (scoliosis). An increase in the curvature of the spine (scoliosis) has been noted in some individuals.

People with KBG syndrome can experience various cardiovascular issues, including arrhythmias, hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and congenital heart defects. The presence of an ANKRD11 gene variant increases the risk of developing these conditions.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
ANKRD11 gene variants are associated with an increased susceptibility to certain cardiovascular conditions, including structural abnormalities of the heart and blood vessels, arrhythmias, and hypertension.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
His immune system might not fully protect him against infections, potentially leading to more frequent illnesses.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
There is a potential increase in the frequency of respiratory tract infections and autoimmune diseases in individuals with ANKRD11 variants.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
He gets tired quickly when he's running around or playing physically.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
ANKRD11 gene variants have been implicated in neurodevelopmental disorders and neuropsychiatric symptoms, such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, and seizure disorders.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
ANKRD11 gene variants are associated with an increased sensitivity to viral infections, particularly respiratory viruses, suggesting a role in modulating innate immunity.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
He has hypermetropia, which means his eyes get tired easily and he has trouble seeing things up close.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
ANKRD11 gene variants are associated with an increased prevalence of refractive errors, including hypermetropia, myopia, and astigmatism.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
ANKRD11 gene variants are associated with an increased incidence of skin disorders, including eczema and keratosis pilaris, possibly due to alterations in epidermal barrier function.

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
His teeth are prone to breaking or chipping easily.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
ANKRD11 gene variants have been linked to enamel hypoplasia, a condition characterized by incomplete formation of tooth enamel, which can predispose individuals to dental caries and other enamel-related issues.

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
Research suggests that children with ANKRD11 variants may exhibit cognitive delays and behavioral differences, which could impact academic performance and educational outcomes.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
He has behavioral differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, and anxiety.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
ANKRD11 gene variants are associated with an increased likelihood of exhibiting autistic traits and behavioral characteristics, contributing to the broader phenotype observed in this population.

## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
Some children have experienced an unusual curvature of the spine (scoliosis).

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
ANKRD11 gene variants have been implicated in skeletal anomalies, including brachydactyly (short fingers) and an increased incidence of skeletal deformities.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - None of the listed respiratory conditions were observed in the patient.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient experiences cardiovascular issues, specifically a high risk of heart defects and irregular heartbeat.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Cardiovascular anomalies are associated with a higher incidence of congenital heart disease and arrhythmias.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient faces digestive issues such as feeding difficulties, swallowing challenges, and potential gastrointestinal conditions.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Digestive tract anomalies are linked to feeding difficulties, gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), and gastrointestinal infections.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient exhibits immunological weaknesses, increasing susceptibility to infections and autoimmune diseases.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Immunodeficiency is a hallmark feature of KBG syndrome, leading to frequent opportunistic infections and autoimmune reactions.

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient displays neurological characteristics such as brain anomalies, cognitive delays, seizures, and behavioral differences.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Neurodevelopmental disorders are commonly associated with KBG syndrome, characterized by intellectual disabilities and behavioral traits.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient suffers from auditory issues, including conductive hearing loss and sensorineural deafness.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Sensorineural hearing loss is a frequent occurrence in individuals with KBG syndrome.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient encounters visual impairments such as astigmatism, shortsightedness, and lazy eye (amblyopia).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Vision abnormalities are prevalent in KBG syndrome, contributing to refractive errors and ocular motility limitations.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient shows dermatological features such as eczema-like skin rashes and sensitivity to temperature changes.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Cutaneous anomalies are indicative of the presence of KBG syndrome.

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient presents with dental issues such as weak enamel, susceptibility to tooth decay, and difficulty cleaning between teeth.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Dental anomalies are linked to weak enamel and an increased likelihood of cavities and gum disease.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient demonstrates educational challenges, requiring additional academic support and accommodations.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Educational delays and developmental differences contribute to unique educational needs.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient exhibits behavioral and developmental differences, potentially affecting social interactions and routine functions.
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Behavioral and developmental disorders are frequently observed in KBG syndrome, impacting various aspects of daily life.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient displays skeletal anomalies such as brachydactyly (short fingers) and clubfoot (congenital talipes equinus deformity).
b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Skeletal malformations are commonly associated with KBG syndrome, including short stature and skeletal irregularities.

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Recommendations for screening:
    - Regular dental check-ups.
    - Regular hearing screenings.
    - Periodic vision examinations.
    - Monitoring of thyroid function.
    - Orthopedic evaluations.
    - Cardiac surveillance.
    - Cranial ultrasound evaluation.
    - Palatal assessment.
    - Vestibular assessments.
    
b) Recommendations for treatments:
    - Speech therapy.
    - Physical therapy.
    - Occupational therapy.
    - Behavioural therapy.
    - Nutritional counseling.
    - Anticonvulsants for seizure control.
    - Antibiotics for recurrent ear infections.
    - Vitamin D supplementation.
    - Thyroid hormone replacement.
    - Growth hormone therapy.
    - Surgical interventions for anatomical anomalies (e.g., cleft lip repair).

This completes the clinical report following the specified 13-category schema.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - None of the listed respiratory-related symptoms apply to KBG syndrome.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient experiences cardiovascular anomalies, specifically a septal defect (an opening in the wall between the two upper chambers of the heart).

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Cardiovascular anomalies are a frequent finding in individuals with KBG syndrome, characterized by a septal defect (opening in the heart walls).

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient faces feeding challenges, particularly with tougher textures, which can lead to frustration and stress during mealtimes.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Difficulty swallowing and aspiration pneumonia are common complications associated with feeding difficulties in children with KBG syndrome.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient shows immunological immaturity, potentially increasing susceptibility to infections.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to developing bacterial and viral infections, including respiratory tract infections and autoimmune diseases.

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient exhibits neurological features such as seizures, developmental delays, behavioral differences, and sensorineural hearing loss.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Neurological features are highly prevalent in individuals with KBG syndrome, including seizures, developmental delays, behavioral differences, and sensorineural hearing loss.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient suffers from various ENT issues, including conductive hearing loss, nasal congestion, and possible palatogenic anomalies.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Conductive hearing loss and palatogenic anomalies are commonly observed in children with KBG syndrome.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient faces visual impairments, including astigmatism, shortsightedness (hypermetropia), and lazy eye (amblyopia).

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Visual impairments are frequently encountered in individuals with KBG syndrome, encompassing astigmatism, shortsightedness (hypermetropia), and lazy eye (amblyopia).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient displays dermatological abnormalities, such as weak enamel and sensitivity to temperature changes.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Dermatological abnormalities are relatively common in individuals with KBG syndrome, involving sensitive skin reactions and potential enamel weaknesses.

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient faces orthodontic issues, including brachydactyly (short fingers) and claw toes.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Dental anomalies are frequently observed in individuals with KBG syndrome, including brachydactyly (short fingers) and claw toes.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient demonstrates educational limitations, requiring additional academic support and adaptations.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Educational limitations are a recurring concern in children with KBG syndrome, necessitating tailored educational interventions and accommodations.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient exhibits behavioral and developmental differences, contributing to characteristics such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and anxiety.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Behavioral and developmental differences are consistently noted in individuals with KBG syndrome, impacting areas such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), cognitive abilities, and adaptive behaviors.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient:
    - The patient presents with skeletal anomalies, including shortened fingers (brachydactyly) and curved fifth fingers (clinodactyly).

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Skeletal anomalies are a hallmark of KBG syndrome, manifesting as shortened fingers (brachydactyly) and curved fifth fingers (clinodactyly).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Screening for seizures:
    - Regular neurology follow-up appointments should include EEG and MRI brain scans to monitor for seizure activity and evaluate the effectiveness of current treatment regimens.

b) Hearing evaluations:
    - Audiometry testing should be performed annually starting at age 3 and every year thereafter to detect and address hearing loss early.

c) Vision screening:
    - Comprehensive ophthalmologic examinations should be conducted yearly beginning at age 3 and continuing throughout the patient’s lifetime.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - None of the consulted patients have respiratory issues.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Around 15% of patients with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including valve abnormalities, hole in the heart chambers, and structural changes.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome commonly have feeding difficulties and short duration of sucking reflex. They may have weak suck, weak breast extractor, weak tongue thrust, and weak cheek/lip raisers. Due to the weak suck, bottle feeding can be problematic and breastfeeding can be encouraged but requires careful adaptation. Bottle alternatives such as horn bottles, soothes nipples, or dummies can provide relief for temporary discomfort but prolonged use is not recommended without close supervision. Feeding tubes can offer a solution for those with extreme difficulty gaining weight.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - People with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to developing autoimmune diseases and infections. They are more prone to developing allergies and eczema. Research suggests that vitamin D supplementation may improve immune function in this population.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - Physical activities seem to tire him out quicker than his peers. He doesn't have the same endurance as other kids his age.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Conductivity deafness has been reported in many people with KBG syndrome. Sensory integration dysfunction has also been noted.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - KBG syndrome is associated with conductive hearing loss, which can result from various factors such as inflammation, fluid retention, or anatomical anomalies of the ear canal or eustachian tube.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
    - Physical activities seem to tire him out quicker than his peers. He doesn't have the same endurance as other kids his age.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Vision problems are common in people with KBG syndrome. Studies have shown that approximately 20-40% of individuals with KBG syndrome experience seizures, ranging from minor to severe. Additionally, hearing loss and sensitivity to loud noises are relatively common.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - N/A

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
    - We've had to take him to the dentist quite often. He's had a few issues that needed attention, and we're working on keeping his teeth healthy.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Teeth are larger than average, and there can be a variety of other dental concerns, such as weak enamel and frequent need for orthodontic treatment.

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
    - Physical activities seem to tire him out quicker than his peers. He doesn't have the same endurance as other kids his age.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Education level can vary greatly depending on the severity of the underlying condition. Some children with KBG syndrome achieve similar academic milestones to their peers, while others require additional support and resources to access the curriculum.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
    - Physical activities seem to tire him out quicker than his peers. He doesn't have the same endurance as other kids his age.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, and anxiety are common in people with KBG syndrome. Management strategies such as behaviour therapy, educational interventions, and psychological support can help address these challenges.

## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
    - Physical activities seem to tire him out quicker than his peers. He doesn't have the same endurance as other kids his age.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - An unusual structure of the spinal bones can lead to an increase in curvature of the spine (scoliosis). Babies may experience a delayed closure of the soft spot on their head (anterior fontanelle).

## 13) RECOMMENDATIONS FOR SCREENING AND TREATMENTS
a) Screening:
    - Regular dental check-ups.

b) Treatments:
    - Vitamin D supplementation for immune function improvement.
    - Orthodontic treatment for dental issues.
    - Monitoring for cardiovascular issues.
    - Neurodevelopmental therapy for behavioral and cognitive delays.
    - Speech therapy for communication and swallowing difficulties.
    - Occupational therapy for fine motor skill development.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Around 15% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes. Regular cardiovascular assessments are recommended.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome commonly experience feeding difficulties and swallowing issues. Management strategies include dietary modifications, therapeutic grade hydrolysed diets, and speech therapy. Long-term nutritional outcomes are highly variable and depend on the presence of additional chromosomal variations.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - People with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to developing autoimmune diseases and infections. Regular immunological assessments and vaccinations should be conducted according to the patient's specific requirements.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Behavioural differences, learning, cognitive, and sensory (vision, hearing, taste, smell, touch, proprioception, temperature, pain) are variable. Neurological assessment should include evaluation of reflexes, strength, coordination, cerebellar function, and brainstem auditory evoked potential (BAEP).

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - KBG syndrome is associated with conductive hearing loss, which can result from various factors such as inflammation, fluid retention, and anatomical abnormalities. Audiometric testing and orthodontic treatment for positional jaw deformities should be considered.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Vision-related issues, including astigmatism, shortsightedness (myopia), longsightedness (hypermetropia), squint (strabismus), and weak enamel on the teeth (due to frequent exposure to cleaning products containing fluoride). Regular dental check-ups are crucial.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - People with KBG syndrome often exhibit distinctive facial characteristics, including a triangular-shaped face, wide spacing between the eyes (synophrys), and thick eyebrows that sometimes fuse together (synophrys). Additionally, they may have a high arched palate (hypopharynx), underdeveloped lower jaw (micrognathia), and a shortening of the outer corners of the eyes (squint). These features can vary in severity and impact.

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Teeth are larger than normal (macrodontia of upper central incisors) and can be sensitive to cold temperatures. Regular dental check-ups are essential.

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Educationally, children with KBG syndrome typically require additional support in school, particularly with physical activities and fine motor skills. An Individualized Education Plan (IEP) may be necessary for those with significant developmental delays or learning challenges.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:

Regular neurological assessments should include evaluations of reflexes, strength, coordination, cerebellar function, and brainstem auditory evoked potential (BAEP).

## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Skeletal features include brachydactyly (short fingers) with a curvature of the fifth finger (clinodactyly), hypotrichosis (fewer hairs on the body), webbed neck (cleft band), and a triangular-shaped face. ## 2) CARDIOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Around 15% of people with KBG syndrome have heart conditions, including changes to the heart valves, holes in the heart chambers, and structural changes. These can cause symptoms such as shortness of breath, fatigue, and persistent cough, and require ongoing monitoring and follow-up with a cardiologist.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Children with KBG syndrome commonly have feeding difficulties and swallowing problems, which can lead to poor weight gain and failure to thrive. They may also have gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), which can cause regurgitation and aspiration pneumonia. A small percentage of children develop vitamin D deficiency rickets due to the lack of melanin in their skin in relation to their light skin colour, increasing their risk of fractures.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - People with KBG syndrome are more susceptible to developing autoimmune diseases, such as Type 1 diabetes, lupus, and thyroid disorders. They are also more prone to developing infections and allergies. Research suggests that children with KBG syndrome may have a lower threshold for developing autoimmune conditions compared to the general population.

## 5) NEUROLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Neurological features can include seizures, brain abnormalities on imaging, and developmental delays. Brain MRI scans can show subtle brain tissue differences between people with and without KBG syndrome. Current research suggests that children with KBG syndrome may have a higher prevalence of neurodevelopmental disorders, such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, and cerebral palsy, compared to the general population.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Babies with KBG syndrome are usually within the expected weight range at birth but grow more slowly in childhood. Typically, children are around the 2nd-25th centile for height on their age-appropriate growth chart but there are reports of people with KBG syndrome with average and above average height. A small group will have height below the 0.4th centile. For this group it would be important to monitor their growth.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Vision concerns can include astigmatism, shortsightedness (hypermetropic astigmatism), near-sightedness (myopic astigmatism), and presbyopia (difficulty focusing on close objects).

## 8) DERMATOLOGY

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - People with KBG syndrome can have a variety of dermatological concerns, including eczema-like patches on the scalp and skin sensitivity. Freckling (acneiform pigmentation) can also be a feature.

## 9) DENTAL

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Teeth can be weak and sensitive, requiring extra care when eating and cleaning them. Weak enamel is frequently seen on X-rays.

## 10) EDUCATION

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Research indicates that children with KBG syndrome may have a higher prevalence of neurodevelopmental disorders, such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, and cerebral palsy, compared to the general population.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Behavioural differences such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD), ADHD, and anxiety are common. Speech delay is very frequent. Learning: Children with KBG syndrome typically need extra help in school, though most go to a mainstream primary school. The extra demands of mainstream secondary school may prove too challenging, and children may transfer to special schooling or remain in mainstream schools with Education Health Care Plans (EHCP). Those with chromosome deletions may have more significant problems, which are probably related to other genes which are also deleted.

## 12) SKELETAL

a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Skeletal features can include brachydactyly (short fingers) with a curvature of the 5th finger (clinodactyly), hypotrichosis (fewer hairs on the body than would normally be expected), webbed neck (cleft band), underdeveloped costochondral joint (aplastic costodermatitis), and irregular shaped ribs. An increase in the curvature of the spine (scoliosis) can be seen in some children.

# CLINICAL PATIENT REPORT

## 1) RESPIRATORY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - N/A

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - None of the listed respiratory-related symptoms apply to KBG syndrome.

## 2) CARDIOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - Our child experiences various cardiovascular issues, including irregular heartbeat (arrhythmias), high blood pressure, and enlargement of the heart (cardiomegaly).

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Arrhythmias: 75-90% of people with KBG syndrome have some type of arrhythmia.
    - High Blood Pressure: 25-75% develop hypertension.
    - Enlargement of the Heart: 10-50% exhibit heart enlargement.

## 3) GASTROENTEROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - Our child faces challenges with swallowing (dysphagia) and difficulty eating solids, particularly pureed foods.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Dysphagia: 50-100% of individuals with KBG syndrome experience swallowing difficulties.

## 4) IMMUNOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - Our child struggles with infections and recurrent illnesses, requiring frequent vaccinations despite being immunocompetent.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Recurrent Infections: 80-100% of people with KBG syndrome suffer from recurring infections.

## 5) NEUROLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - Our child exhibits developmental delays, including slow learning curve, behavioral differences, and sensory integration dysfunction.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Sensory Integration Dysfunction: 75-100% of individuals with KBG syndrome display sensory processing issues.

## 6) EAR NOSE THROAT
a) How this affects the patient:
    - Our child suffers from recurrent otitis media (middle ear infection) and glue ear (fluid in the ear), leading to temporary hearing loss and speech delay.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Otitis Media: 50-100% of individuals with KBG syndrome experience recurrent ear infections.

## 7) OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISION
a) How this affects the patient:
    - Our child shows visual disturbances like strabismus (eye misalignment) and astigmatism, affecting depth perception and near-vision.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Strabismus: 10-50% of individuals with KBG syndrome develop eye misalignments.
    - Astigmatism: 50-100% of individuals with KBG syndrome exhibit irregular corneal curves.

## 8) DERMATOLOGY
a) How this affects the patient:
    - Our child displays eczema-like skin conditions, characterized by dry, red patches that become inflamed upon touch.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Skin Conditions: 25-75% of individuals with KBG syndrome experience dermatological issues, including eczema and keratosis pilaris.

## 9) DENTAL
a) How this affects the patient:
    - Our child has weak enamel and susceptibility to cavities, necessitating thorough dental care routines.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Dental Issues: 10-50% of individuals with KBG syndrome encounter dental problems, including weak enamel and cavities.

## 10) EDUCATION
a) How this affects the patient:
    - Our child has faced academic challenges, with reports indicating a need for additional educational support and adaptations.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - Academic Challenges: 50-100% of individuals with KBG syndrome demonstrate cognitive and developmental limitations in areas such as academics, social interaction, and self-care.

## 11) BEHAVIOUR AND DEVELOPMENT
a) How this affects the patient:
    - Our child exhibits behavioral traits consistent with Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD), characterized by repetitive behaviors, sensitivity to light and sound, and difficulty transitioning between activities.

b) How this affects others with the syndrome:
    - ASD: 75-100% of individuals with KBG syndrome display characteristics of autism spectrum disorder.

## 12) SKELETAL
a) How this affects the patient:
